nota: Words of this language that look borrowed from another language but do not exist there with that meaning, grouped by the language they imitate.

parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from aerobics. While aerobic exists in English to refer to aerobics, it is an adjective and not a noun.
Borrowed from French autocar, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English autocar. By surface analysis, auto- + car.

parole.significato: hitchhiking, hitch-hiking, hitching, thumbing a ride
parole.testo: Borrowed from French auto-stop, and this a pseudo-anglicism, from auto- (relating to cars) + stop (hitchiking).
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from balcón + -ing.
Borrowed from English beatbox. The sense "beatboxing" is a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English beatboxing.
Borrowed from French body, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English bodysuit.
Unadapted borrowing from English bowling. The sense "bowling alley" is a pseudo-anglicism derived from an ellipsis of English bowling alley, borrowed from French bowling.
Borrowed from English box. Doublet of buje. The sense "boxing" is a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English boxing.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from boy.

parole.significato: braces (a device worn on the teeth to straighten them)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English bracket. The sense "braces" is a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English bracket.
Borrowed from French break, and this a pseudo-anglicism, from earlier break de chasse, from English shooting brake.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from bungy jumping.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from a humorous Spanish-to-English calque of por la cara.
Borrowed from French basket, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English basketball.

parole.significato: Boxer (a participant in the Boxer Rebellion in China)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English boxer. The sense "boxer shorts" is a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English boxer shorts; note that while boxer does exist in English to refer to boxer shorts, it only exists as
Borrowed from English camping. The sense "campsite" is a pseudo-anglicism.
Clipping of videoclip; pseudo-anglicism.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from cross country. -cross exists in English to refer to cross country, but only as a suffix.
Borrowed from French dancing, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English dance + -ing.
Borrowed from French dripping, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English drip + -ing.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from edredón (“duvet”) + English -ing. Term coined in the reality show Gran Hermano.
Borrowed from French smoking, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English smoking jacket.
Borrowed from French fixing, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English fixing.

parole.significato: jogging (as a form of exercise), running
parole.testo: Borrowed from French footing, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English foot (“foot, to walk”) + -ing.
Borrowed from English freaky. The "nerd" and "geek" senses are a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English freaky and influenced by English freak.

parole.significato: synonym of de perdidos al río
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from a Spanish-to-English calque of de perdidos al río. Most famously used as the title of the humorous satirical book From Lost to the River by Ignacio Ochoa and Federico Ló
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from gas car and influenced by French car.
Pseudo-anglicism, from goma (“rubber, after the string”) + -ing.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English holding company.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from home office. Compare German Homeoffice.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English lineout.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from living room. Borrowing directly from French living is unlikely because this word is only used in the Southern Cone.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from mailing list.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English sweatpants.

parole.significato: car park, (North America) parking lot, parking garage
parole.testo: Borrowed from French parking, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English parking.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from pass + ball.
Borrowed from French playback, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English playback.
Pseudo-anglicism, from puente (“bridge”) + -ing.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of reality show.
Borrowed from French recordman, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from record + -man.
Pseudo-anglicism, clipping of English relaxation or erroneous borrowing of English relax.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from renting.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English right fielder.

parole.significato: of course, for sure, certainly (affirmative answer)
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from right + true.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from rolling.

parole.significato: shopping (the leisure activity of going shopping)
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from English shopping. The sense "shopping center" is a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English shopping center.
Pseudo-anglicism, the first sense derived from English skateboard, and the second from English skateboarding. Note that the English noun skate only refers to an instance of skateboarding, and not the
Borrowed from French slip, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English slip.
Unadapted borrowing from English snorkel. The sense "snorkeling" is a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English snorkeling.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from surfing. Note that the English noun surf only refers to an instance of surfing, and not the activity itself.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from taxi + boy.
Borrowed from English tennis. The sense "tennis show" is a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English tennis shoe.
Borrowed from French top-modèle, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English top + English model.

parole.significato: dolly, camera dolly (a specialized piece of film equipment resembling a little cart on which a camera is mounted)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French travelling, and this a pseudo-anglicism, from English travel + -ing.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from two bases.
Borrowed from French vidéoclip, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from English videoclip.
Borrowed from French water, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English water closet. Doublet of onda.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from windsurfing. Note that the English noun windsurf only refers to an instance of windsurfing, and not the activity itself.
Borrowed from English indoor. The sense "indoor football" is a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English indoor football.

Pseudo-Latinism, derived from idem (“same”) + potentia (“the quality of having power”), coined as a calque of English idempotence, equivalent to ídem + potencia. Cognate with Catalan idempotència, Fre
Borrowed from English in silico, and this a pseudo-Latinism; see that entry for more.
Borrowed from English lorem ipsum, and this a pseudo-Latinism; see that entry for more.
Pseudo-Italianism, constructed from Italian pippione (“squab, young pigeon”) and -olo (diminutive), the former from Latin pīpiōnem (“squab, young pigeon”), ultimately onomatopoeic.
Pseudo-Italianism, derived from the Italian phrase testa di ferro (“iron head”). Compare Asturian testaferru, Leonese testaferre, and Portuguese testa de ferro.
Borrowed from English Häagen-Dazs, and this a pseudo-loan from Danish; see that entry for more.

parole.significato: hentai (a work of anime or manga—Japanese cartoon art, respectively animated and static—that contains pornography)
parole.testo: Borrowed from English hentai, and this a pseudo-Japonism derived from Japanese 変態(へんたい) (hentai); see that entry for more.
